verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents adding experiment rules to feature flags that hash users into one of the experiment variations. Its results page reports a per-variation 'Chance to Win', highlighting a clear winner in green once it passes 95%, computed against warehouse-defined goal metrics by a Bayesian/Frequentist stats engine. A community user confirms running flag-based A/B tests hands-on. missing for 10: explicit documentation of multivariate (more than two arm) tests beyond the plural 'variations' wording, and independent hands-on corroboration of the winner/metrics analysis.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can run A/B and multivariate experiments on flags and see which variation wins on my metrics

citations.quote: you can add an experiment rule to a feature that will randomly assign the users based on some hashing attribute into one of your experiment variations.
Chance to Win tells you the probability that the variation is better. Anything above 95% ... is highlighted green indicating a very clear winner.
Define Fact Tables and metrics so GrowthBook can compute experiment results from your warehouse.
